subject: Electrical Engineering
title: Stator and Rotor: The Two Halves
description: A fast breakdown of Stator and Rotor: The Two Halves for builders.

hook.text: Every motor has a part that stays still and a part that spins. Stator and rotor.

buildup.text: The stator creates a magnetic field. The rotor carries conductors or magnets that interact.

discovery.text: The air gap between them is critical — smaller gaps mean stronger magnetic coupling.

twist.text: Some motors flip the roles: the outer part spins. These are called outrunner motors.

climax.text: Drone propellers use outrunner motors — high torque at low speed, no gearbox needed.

punchline.text: One part stands, one part spins — together they make motion from magnetism.

quiz.question: What is an outrunner motor?
options: A motor where the outer casing (rotor) spins while the inner part stays fixed
A motor that runs faster than its rated speed
A motor designed to operate only outdoors
